core_obligations: Assume the formal fibres of every finite free extension are regular and take primes q inside p together with a finite purely inseparable extension L of the residue field (proof lines 12269-12274).
Choose a finite free extension of the ring realising L at a prime over q, using the cited existence statement (proof lines 12274-12278).
Use the product decomposition of the completion after this finite extension to rewrite the algebra whose regularity must be checked as a product of completed local rings (proof lines 12278-12292).
Read off regularity from the hypothesis, conclude that the ring is a G-ring, and quote the converse from the quasi-finite going-up statement (proof lines 12292-12302).
proof_roadmap: Set up the test data (proof lines 12269-12274).
Realise the residue field extension by a finite free extension (proof lines 12274-12278).
Decompose the completed algebra and apply the hypothesis (proof lines 12278-12292).
Conclude and quote the converse (proof lines 12292-12303).
difficulty_reason: The lemma replaces the G-ring condition by a test over finite free extensions, and the proof is a 35-line argument that transports regularity of formal fibres across such an extension. Given primes q inside p and a finite purely inseparable extension of the residue field, it chooses a finite free extension of the ring realising that extension at a prime over q, uses the product decomposition of the completion after a finite extension to write the algebra to be tested as a product of completed local rings of the extension, and reads regularity off the hypothesis; the converse is quoted from the statement that the G-ring property goes up along quasi-finite maps. The construction of the finite free extension and the product decomposition are the two steps with content, and both are displayed.
